title: Assistant credits top up - now available
raw_evidence_quote: Starting today, if you’re on n8n Cloud (Starter or Pro) and you run out of Assistant credits, you can buy more and keep building.
source_text:
Starting today, if you’re on n8n Cloud (Starter or Pro) and you run out of Assistant credits, you can buy more and keep building. 
 Being able to top up has been one of the most common requests we’ve heard since we launched n8n Assistant. Until now, running out meant waiting for your allowance to reset on the 1st of the month, or upgrading your plan. Neither is a great option when you’re halfway through building a workflow. 
          image-1  1600×934 206 KB         
  The new Assistant credits tab  
   How top-ups work 
 Your plan still includes a monthly allowance of Assistant credits that resets on the 1st of the month. Top-ups are extra credits on top of that, and they’re optional. 
 You can add extra credits in two ways: 
 
  Top up manually.  Pick a credit package whenever you need one. 
  Turn on auto top-up.  Choose the extra-credit balance that triggers a top-up and the balance to refill to. A monthly limit, on by default, caps how much auto top-up can charge in a month. 
 
 The Assistant always uses your included credits first, and only moves on to extra credits once those run out. Extra credits carry over from month to month and expire 12 months after you buy them. 
          image-2  1600×922 217 KB         
  Manual Top Up  
   See where your credits go 
 The new  Assistant credits  tab in the Cloud admin dashboard shows: 
 
 Your balance, split into included and extra credits 
 A spend chart for the last 24 hours, 7 days, or 30 days 
 Which users on your instance use the most credits 
 Your top-up history 
 
 In the editor, the Assistant panel shows how many credits the current conversation has used, and warns you when you’re down to 10%. 
            2000×664 107 KB         
   We’ve updated your monthly credits 
 If you’re on Starter or Pro, you’ll notice that your monthly credit allowance has changed. 
 For most people, the updated allowance will go further than before. That comes down to some improvements we’ve made: 
 
  A newer, more capable model.  We’ve moved everyone to a newer model, so the Assistant needs fewer credits to do the same work. 
  One standard credit value.  Now that you can buy credits, a credit needs a fixed price. We recalibrated credits so they’re worth the same on every paid plan, and set each plan’s allowance to match. 
  Improvements under the hood.  We’ve optimized how the Assistant works internally, so it gets more done with each request. 
 
   How many credits does it take to build a workflow? 
 That’s the question we get most often, and there’s no single answer. It depends on the request: longer conversations, more complex workflows, and debugging sessions use more credits than short, focused requests. No two prompts will cost the same, due to non-deterministic LLM behavior and different surrounding context. 
 What we can provide is a is a sense of the range to expect. Here are what a few typical requests use today: 
 
  A quick question  [10-20 Credits]
 
 “What authentication methods for Slack does n8n Support?” 
 
 
  A simple workflow or fix from one prompt  [50-100 credits]
 
 “Once a day, check the weather in Berlin using a free weather API and email me the forecast.” 
 
 
  A larger build with explicit testing, or a longer debugging session  [300-600 credits]
 
 “Before building, research the current docs for free keyless APIs for geocoding, weather forecasts, country info and exchange rates, and pick three real destinations with very different weather this week so each one lands in a different trip category. Then build a “Travel Weather Briefing” workflow: a form asks for a city, travel dates and home currency, the APIs above gather the data, writes packing tips, labels the trip Hot, Cold, Wet or Mild, and each briefing is saved to a Data Table. Post the briefing to a Slack channel, show it on the form’s completion page. Ensure you handle errors such as unknown cities or currencies, and test the workflow with the three cities you researched.” 
 
 
 
 These ranges will change as we keep improving the Assistant and the models behind it, so treat them as a rough guide. One tip that definitely helps: specific prompts use fewer credits than open-ended ones. 
   A few things to know 
 
  Credits are shared across your instance.  Everyone on the instance draws from the same balance. If five people on your team use the Assistant, they’re all using the same pool, and the top users view shows who’s using what. 
  Only the instance owner can top up.  Topping up also requires an active paid plan. 
  Your workflows keep running.  Running a workflow never uses Assistant credits, even if the Assistant built it. Only your conversations with the Assistant do. 
  Assistant credits and Gateway credits are separate.  Assistant credits pay for your conversations with the Assistant. Gateway credits pay for the AI model calls your workflows and agents make when they run. Topping up one doesn’t add to the other. 
  Free trials include a one-time allowance.  Free trials get 800 credits. Top-ups aren’t available during a trial, so you’ll need to upgrade to a paid plan to get more. 
  Self-hosted n8n doesn’t use Assistant credits.  The Assistant runs on your own model provider account instead. 
 
 For all the details, check out the  Assistant credits docs . 
 Feel free to reply to this post with questions …
risk: No verified buyer awareness gap or willingness to pay; add-on credits can increase spend. Never resell access or shared accounts.
next_action: Ask an existing consenting Cloud operator who hits credit limits whether they know the top-up option and need a bounded cost/usage audit. Do not pitch without buyer demand.

info_edge.novelty: Cloud Starter/Pro Assistant credits can be topped up instead of waiting or upgrading the base plan.
info_edge.information_gap: Hypothesis only: some operators may still believe upgrading is the only way to continue. No awareness interviews conducted.
info_edge.target_buyer: n8n Cloud Starter/Pro teams demonstrably constrained by Assistant monthly credits
info_edge.monetization_path: Authorized fixed-scope usage/plan comparison audit, only after paid demand evidence; no resale.
info_edge.decay_window: 14 days from Oct 1 announcement for discovery validation; widespread docs reduce gap quickly.
info_edge.legality_check: Public official source; ordinary plan use only, no account sharing, resale or policy evasion.

verification_sources.quote: Starting today, if you’re on n8n Cloud (Starter or Pro) and you run out of Assistant credits, you can buy more and keep building.
verification_sources.method: Public primary web reader re-read 2026-10-14; crawl today; original Oct 1 event unchanged

info_edge.validation_action: Before the Oct 15 discovery expiry, distinguish Assistant versus Gateway credits and top-up versus upgrade in one comparison note. Prepare an awareness question for an existing consenting Cloud operator; do not buy credits or assume a paying buyer.

title: Haiku 5.5 launch: cost-sensitive automation model evaluation
raw_evidence_quote: On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.
source_text: On average, it now costs around 75% less to run.
derived_interpretation: Current verified technical change, not yet verified information asymmetry.
suggested_price_range: USD 100–200 test audit; no buyer budget verified
first_message: Are you still using Haiku 4.5 for repetitive classification? Would a measured cost/quality comparison help?
risk: No evidence that few target buyers know; tokenization, long prompts, quality, retry and migration costs may erase savings.
next_action: In 24–48 hours ask three consenting operators about current model/spend/awareness; test 30 anonymized cases before proposing a paid audit.
